source_text: Sed quoniam ita mulieris nomen usurpant, ut non putent competere illud nisi ei soli quae virum passa sit, probari a nobis oportet proprietatem eius vocabuli ad sexum ipsum, non ad gradum sexus pertinere, quo communiter etiam virgines censeantur. Cum hoc genus secundi hominis a deo factum est in adiutorium hominis, femina illa, statim mulier est cognominata, adhuc felix, adhuc digna paradiso, adhuc virgo. Vocabitur, inquit, mulier. Habes itaque nomen, non dico iam virgini commune, sed proprium, quod a principio virgo sortita est. Sed ingeniose quidam de futuro volunt dictum, Vocabitur mulier, quasi quae hoc futura esset, cum virginitatem resignasset, quoniam et adiecit, Propterea relinquet homo patrem et matrem, et conglutinabitur mulieri suae, et erunt duo in una carne. Ostendant igitur primo, ubi sit subtilitas ista, si de futuro mulier cognominata est, quod interea vocabulum acceperit. Non potest enim sine vocabulo praesentis qualitatis suae fuisse. Ceterum quale est, ut quae in futurum vocaretur nomine designato, in praesenti nihil cognominaretur? Omnibus animalibus Adam nomina imposuit et nemini ex futura condicione, sed ex praesenti institutione, cui condicio quaecunque serviret, hoc appellata quod a primordio voluit. Quid ergo tunc vocabatur? Atquin quotienscumque in scriptura nominatur, mulier appellatur, antequam nupta, et nunquam virgo, cum virgo. Hoc nomen tum unum illi fuit, et quando nihil prophetico modo dictum est. Nam cum scriptura refert fuisse nudos duos, Adam et mulierem eius, nec hoc de futuro sapit, quasi mulierem dixerit eius in praesagio (??)xoris, sed quoniam et innupta illius mulier, ut de substantia ipsius. Hoc, inquit, os ex ossibus meis et caro ex carne mea vocabitur mulier. Hinc ergo tacita conscientia naturae ipsa divinitas animae in usum sermonis eduxit nescientibus hominibus, sicut et alia multa, quae ex scriptura fieri et dici solere alibi poterimus ostendere, uti mulieres nostras dicamus uxores, quamquam et improprie quaedam loquamur. Nam et Graeci, qui magis vocabulo mulieris in uxore utuntur, alia habent propria vocabula uxoris. Sed malo hunc usum ad scripturae testimonium deputare. Ubi enim duo in unam carnem efficiuntur per matrimonii nexum, caro ex carne et os ex ossibus vocatur secundum originem mulier eius ex cuius substantia incipit censeri facta uxor. Ita mulier non natura nomen est uxoris, sed uxor condicione nomen est mulieris. Denique mulier et non uxor dici potest, non mulier autem uxor dici non potest, quia nec esse. Constituto igitur nomine novae feminae, quod est mulier, et explicito quod prius fuit, id est nomine assignato, convertit iam ad propheticam rationem, uti diceret, Propter hanc relinquet homo patrem et matrem. Adeo separatum est nomen a prophetia, quantum et ab ipsa persona, ut non utique de ipsa Eva dixerit, sed in illas feminas futuras, quas in matrice generis feminini nominarit. Alioquin non Adam relicturus erat patrem et matrem, quos non habebat, propter Evam. Ergo non ad Evam pertinet, quia nec ad Adam, quod prophetice dictum est. De maritorum enim condicione praedictum, qui ob mulierem parentes suos erant relicturi, quod in Evam cadere non potuit, quia nec in Adam. Si ita res est, apparet non propter futurum mulierem cognominatam, ad quam futurum non pertinebat. Eo accedit, quod ipse rationem eius nominis edidit. Cum enim dixisset, Vocabitur mulier, Quoniam ex viro suo sumpta est, ait, et ipso adhuc virgine. Sed dicemus et de viri nomine suo loco. Nemo itaque nomen ad prophetiam interpretetur, quod ex alia significatione deductum est, praesertim cum appareat, ubi de futuro nomen acceperit, illic scilicet, ubi Eva cognominatur, personali iam vocabulo, quia naturale praecesserat. Si enim Eva mater viventium est, ecce ex futuro cognominatur, ecce uxor et non virgo praenuntiatur. Hoc erit vocabulum nupturae; ex nupta enim mater. Ita hic quoque ostenditur non de futuro mulierem tunc nominatam, quae postmodum acceptura erat futurae condicionis suae nomen. Responsum satis est ad hanc partem.
thought_title: The name 'woman' belongs to the sex, not to marriage
orientation: Tertullian is answering opponents who claim the word 'woman' applies only to a married woman, and he is proving from Genesis that Eve was called 'woman' while still a virgin.
pass_a_gloss: But since they seize upon the name of woman in such a way that they do not think it belongs except to her alone who has experienced a man, it must be proved by us that the proper meaning of that word belongs to the sex itself, not to the degree of the sex, by which virgins also are commonly counted. When this kind of second human being was made by God as a helper for the human being, that female, immediately she is named woman, still happy, still worthy of paradise, still a virgin. She will be called, he says, woman. You have therefore a name, I do not say now common to a virgin, but proper, which from the beginning a virgin obtained. But some cleverly want it said about the future, She will be called woman, as if she would be this when she had unsealed her virginity, since he also added, For this reason a man will leave father and mother, and will be joined to his woman, and the two will be in one flesh. Let them show therefore first, where this subtlety is, if she was named woman from the future, what name she received in the meantime. For she could not have been without a name for her present quality. Otherwise what sort of thing is it, that she who would be called in the future by a designated name, in the present was called by nothing? Adam imposed names on all animals and to no one from a future condition, but from present constitution, to which whatever condition served, this he called what he wanted from the beginning. What therefore was she called then? But indeed as often as she is named in Scripture, she is called woman, before being married, and never virgin, when she was a virgin. This name was then her only one, and when nothing was said in a prophetic manner. For when Scripture reports that the two were naked, Adam and his woman, it does not savor this about the future, as if it had said his woman in a foretelling of a wife, but because she was also unmarried as his woman, as from his substance. This, he says, is bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh; she will be called woman. From here therefore the silent awareness of nature, the divinity of the soul itself, brought out into the use of speech without humans knowing, just as also many other things, which we will be able to show elsewhere are accustomed to be done and said from Scripture, so that we call our women wives, although we also say some things improperly. For the Greeks too, who use the word for woman more for a wife, have other proper words for wife. But I prefer to count this usage as testimony of Scripture. For where two are made into one flesh through the bond of marriage, flesh from flesh and bone from bones is called, according to origin, his woman, from whose substance she begins to be counted as made a wife. Thus woman is not by nature the name of a wife, but wife is by condition the name of a woman. Finally woman and not wife can be said, but not woman, wife cannot be said, because it cannot be. Therefore when the name of the new female was established, which is woman, and what was before was explained, that is, with the name assigned, he turns now to the prophetic reasoning, so that he would say, For this reason a man will leave father and mother. So separated is the name from prophecy, as much as from the person herself, that he did not speak at all about Eve herself, but about those future females, whom he would name in the womb of the female race. Otherwise Adam was not going to leave father and mother, whom he did not have, because of Eve. Therefore it does not pertain to Eve, because neither to Adam, what was said prophetically. For it was foretold about the condition of husbands, who were going to leave their parents because of a woman, which could not fall upon Eve, because neither upon Adam. If the matter is so, it appears that she was not named woman because of a future, to which the future did not pertain. To this is added, that he himself produced the reason for her name. For when he had said, She will be called woman, Because she was taken from her man, he says, and he himself still a virgin. But we will speak also about the name of man in its place. Let no one therefore interpret the name toward prophecy, which was derived from another signification, especially since it appears, where she received a name from the future, there of course, where she is named Eve, now by a personal name, because the natural one had preceded. For if Eve is mother of the living, behold she is named from the future, behold she is foretold as wife and not virgin. This will be the name of one about to marry; for from a married woman she is mother. Thus here also it is shown that she was not then named woman from the future, who afterward was going to receive the name of her future condition. The response is enough for this part.

pass_b_english: But since they seize upon the name “woman” in such a way that they think it belongs only to one who has experienced a man, we must prove that the proper force of that word belongs to the sex itself, not to a degree of the sex, so that virgins are also commonly counted under it. When this second kind of human being was made by God as a helper for man, that female was immediately named woman—still blessed, still worthy of paradise, still a virgin. “She shall be called woman,” Scripture says (Genesis 2:23). So you have a name that I do not say is merely common to a virgin, but proper to her, which a virgin received from the beginning.

But some cleverly want this to have been said about the future: “She shall be called woman,” as if she would become this when she had unsealed her virginity, since Scripture also added, “For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and will be joined to his woman, and the two will be in one flesh” (Genesis 2:24). Let them first show where this subtlety lies: if she was named woman with reference to the future, what name did she receive in the meantime? For she could not have been without a name for her present condition. What kind of reasoning is it that one who would be called by a designated name in the future was called nothing in the present? Adam gave names to all the animals, and to none of them from a future condition, but from their present constitution; whatever condition might serve it, each was called what he willed from the beginning. What then was she called at that time?

But every time she is named in Scripture, she is called woman before she is married, and never virgin, even though she was a virgin. This name was her only one then, and it was not spoken in a prophetic manner. For when Scripture reports that the two were naked, Adam and his woman (Genesis 2:25), this does not have a future sense, as if it called her his woman as a foretelling of a wife, but because she was also his woman while unmarried, since she came from his own substance. “This,” he says, “is bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh; she shall be called woman” (Genesis 2:23). From this, then, the soul’s own divinity, through nature’s silent awareness, brought this usage into common speech without people knowing it—as with many other things that we can show elsewhere are customarily done and said from Scripture—so that we call our women wives, although we also speak some things improperly. For the Greeks too, who use the word for woman more often for a wife, have other proper words for wife. But I prefer to count this usage as testimony from Scripture.

For where two are made into one flesh through the bond of marriage, flesh from flesh and bone from bones is called, according to origin, his woman, from whose substance she begins to be reckoned as having become a wife. Thus woman is not by nature the name of a wife, but wife is by condition the name of a woman. In short, a woman can be called woman and not wife, but one who is not a woman cannot be called a wife, because she cannot be one So when the name of the new female was established—which is woman—and what was prior was made explicit, that is, the assigned name, he now turns to the prophetic reasoning, so as to say, “On account of her a man will leave his father and mother” (Genesis 2:24). The name is so separate from the prophecy, as much as from the person herself, that he did not speak about Eve herself, but about those future females whom he named in the womb of the female race. Otherwise Adam was not going to leave a father and mother, whom he did not have, because of Eve. Therefore what was said prophetically does not pertain to Eve, because it does not pertain to Adam either. It was foretold about the condition of husbands, who would leave their parents because of a woman—which could not fall upon Eve, because it could not fall upon Adam.

If this is so, it is clear that she was not named woman on account of a future which did not pertain to her. To this is added the fact that he himself gave the reason for her name. For when he had said, “She shall be called woman,” he said, “because she was taken from her man” (Genesis 2:23)—and he himself was still a virgin. But we will speak about the man’s name in its proper place. Let no one, then, interpret the name as prophecy, since it was derived from another meaning, especially when it is clear where she received a name from the future—there, of course, where she is named Eve, now with a personal name, because the natural one had preceded. For if Eve is the mother of the living (Genesis 3:20), behold, she is named from the future; behold, she is foretold as a wife and not a virgin. This will be the name of one about to marry; for from a married woman comes a mother. So here too it is shown that she was not then named woman from the future, since she would later receive the name of her future condition. This answer is sufficient for that part.

problems.quote: but a wife cannot be called wife and not woman, because she cannot be one
problems.source_quote: non mulier autem uxor dici non potest, quia nec esse
problems.why: English reverses the subject; the Latin says a woman cannot be called wife, not that a wife cannot be called wife.
problems.fix: but a woman cannot be called wife, because she is not one.
problems.ruling: Latin 'non mulier autem uxor dici non potest' means 'a woman cannot be called wife'; English wrongly says 'a wife cannot be called wife,' reversing subject.

problems.source_quote: non mulier autem uxor dici non potest, quia nec esse

problems.quote: the silent awareness of nature itself led the soul’s own divinity into common speech
problems.source_quote: tacita conscientia naturae ipsa divinitas animae in usum sermonis eduxit
problems.why: Subject and means are swapped. The divinity of the soul is the agent, acting through nature's silent awareness. The English makes the awareness lead the divinity.
problems.fix: the very divinity of the soul, through nature's silent awareness, brought it into common speech

problems.quote: whatever condition each one served, it was called what it was from the beginning
problems.source_quote: cui condicio quaecunque serviret, hoc appellata quod a primordio voluit
problems.why: The later condition serves the name Adam willed; English reverses that and drops his will.
problems.fix: Whatever condition might serve that name, each was called what he willed from the beginning.
problems.ruling: "cui condicio quaecunque serviret, hoc appellata quod a primordio voluit": the condition serves the name Adam willed. English reverses this and drops "voluit".

problems.quote: she was not named woman because of a future to which the future did not pertain
problems.source_quote: non propter futurum mulierem cognominatam, ad quam futurum non pertinebat
problems.why: “Ad quam” is the woman: the future prophecy did not apply to her, not to “a future.”
problems.fix: She was not named woman on account of the future, for the future did not pertain to her.
problems.ruling: "ad quam futurum non pertinebat": "quam" is the woman, so the future did not pertain to her. English "a future to which the future did not pertain" is nonsense.

problems.quote: and she was still a virgin at the time
problems.why: “Ipso” agrees with the man: he, not she, was still a virgin when she was named.
problems.fix: And he himself was still a virgin.
problems.ruling: "ipso adhuc virgine" agrees with the man ("viro suo"), so Adam was still a virgin. English wrongly says she was.
